title: Questions that reveal
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What question would tell you most about someone, without making them feel hunted?

In an interview, Jose said, we have so little time to analyze somebody. You better be good at the questions you ask. You don't want to ask like some intelligence agent, in a threatening way. You want to be very conversational.

A student said: I would ask more questions and talk about myself. Another said: if the answer is too romantic, that is a good sign to move to a harder question, like: what was the big challenge you faced and how did you overcome it? What is one you couldn't overcome?
Jose said you can preface it with a disclaimer: do you mind if I don't use an orthodox way to interview, and we just talk? That is preparing the territory.

A student suggested: describe a time when you were unable to provide the value you thought you could bring to a situation. If somebody romanticizes what they have done, it makes them uncomfortable because they didn't rehearse that.

Another said: tell me about your failures and how you worked them out. Jose said: those are very good. Give me three of the most successful moments of your life. That will tell you a lot about a person.
Jose said you should have five or six revealing questions that help you filter. Everybody will have their own style and selection.

Jose said that people who don't acknowledge the negative hide from it, blame their external environment, and say: the economy did this. That is the person who victimizes themselves. Imagine an investor who invests in you and you say: we lost all the money because of the economy.
A student said: they never think they are in the wrong. Even a simple shift to the idea that they could be wrong makes them defensive. Jose said: people who don't apologize are another sign.
A student asked: do you look at it as someone can change, or that people come as they are? If they don't acknowledge any room to change, that is an early indicator.
What would you ask, and how would you ask it so that the person feels respected?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write five questions you would ask a possible partner.
Write how you would say them so they feel respected.
Write the answer that would worry you.
Write what you would want to hear about their failures.
Write three of your own most successful moments.

check.q: What kind of interview did Jose say to aim for?
What did a student suggest asking about?
choices: A time they could not provide the value they thought they could

check.q: What did Jose say about people who blame their environment?
choices: They victimize themselves, and that is a warning sign

recap: Ask conversational, revealing questions. Listen for blame and for no apology.
